summary: Adds tenant-scoped outbound proxy routing for SSO, with portal and headless configuration.
userImpact: Organizations can route backend OIDC requests through an approved proxy without changing engine or other tenants' traffic.

instructions: Run migration 1700000000134 before rolling out the new runtime. Pooled PostgreSQL deployments use the separately credentialed schema-epoch v4 owner job.
Existing tenants preserve runtime routing until explicitly migrated; new tenants receive Direct.
Before enabling Cloud proxies, qualify the target release/shard route, drain incompatible runtimes and reject incompatible release fallbacks.

configuration: Adds approved SSO proxy profiles and tenant connection selection with source ownership.

changes: Adds tenant and operator SSO connection configuration and diagnostic contracts.

notes: Adds nullable SSO connection/catalogue JSON columns to existing settings and tenant policy tables; PostgreSQL pooled schema-epoch ceiling advances to 0134.
No new runtime table privileges. DOWN refuses populated scoped settings; older schema-epoch runtimes reject the new ledger.

security: Proxy failures never trigger direct fallback; profile selection is tenant-scoped and approved by platform operators.
Refreshes pinned backend/frontend Chainguard runtime bases and requires patched ca-certificates-bundle and libcurl-openssl4 versions for CVE-2026-111943 and CVE-2026-92392.
knownLimitations: HTTP CONNECT without proxy authentication only; private network connectivity is provisioned separately.
Cloud control-plane release compatibility remains an operator-owned rollout prerequisite.
Connection tests verify network/discovery/JWKS reachability; a real sign-in must verify client credentials, MFA and permissions.
The first version limits a catalogue to 32 profiles and 256 distinct assigned scopes.
rollback: Restore reviewed prior connection configuration before downgrading tenants that require scoped proxy routing.
validation: Shared, backend and frontend TypeScript checks and ESLint pass. Full backend/frontend unit suites pass 3,926 and 1,586 tests respectively.
SSO service, real TLS/CONNECT transport, API authorization, signed-state/release-fence, configuration-bundle lifecycle and UI tests pass.
Full identity local suite and security suite, authorization structure/inventory and 128 authorization PR tests pass using owned local PostgreSQL.
All seven pull-request deployment-evidence lanes pass locally, including the complete audited SSO administration route inventory. This does not replace external release acceptance.
PostgreSQL forced-RLS/identity integration passes; the repaired session-race fixture passes all 45 tests.
All five database adapters pass the migration/upgrade/retry/schema-equivalence matrix as a local development run, not a clean release candidate receipt.

The exact rebuilt, scanned application images pass the disposable PostgreSQL protocol rehearsal: SCIM HTTP, OIDC, Entra-compatible OIDC, SAML and LDAP; proxy activated through UI and 37 CONNECT tunnels observed.
The technical guide Mermaid sequence diagram renders in light and dark themes. Helm/schema-epoch/receipt/package-version contract checks pass.

Fresh pinned Trivy 0.72.0 scans on 21 October 2026 pass for both rebuilt Linux arm64 application images: zero unignored CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/UNKNOWN vulnerabilities and zero secret findings, with the committed ignore policy unchanged. SBOMs are retained locally; other architectures require their own image qualification.

Docker/runtime and configuration contracts pass; CI/release contracts pass and the self-validating ci-complete aggregate. Corrects stale ownership/tool-removal expectations, inline pnpm-pin parsing and the plugin-manager example version.

The compiled backend starts and returns healthy against a fresh, owned Oracle XE 21 fixture. The backend explicitly owns the existing IP-address parser dependency used by its compiled SSO transport; dependency-boundary regression contracts pass.
The non-publishing release authorization canary passes 12 scenarios, including the actual candidate verifier's rejection of a missing fixture; no publication or registry writes.

The disposable pooled-tenant browser scenario passes organization discovery, segregated OIDC/SAML/LDAP sign-in, tenant permissions and plugin lifecycle with a restricted PostgreSQL role and 31 forced-RLS tenant tables. The provider assertion targets its visible table cell rather than the proxy selector option.
